## Title

::: {.value-box title="Bibbles" value="60"}
Title above the value
:::

::: {.value-box title="Styled" title-color="yellow" title-font-size="1.4rem" title-extra-style="text-transform:uppercase;" value="61"}
Title with its own colour, size and style hook
:::

A title has to sit above the value/details row rather than become a third item
in it, so this combination gets an extra wrapper.

::: {.value-box title="Rowed" value-position="left" value="62"}
Title above a left-positioned value
:::

Without a title there must be no wrapper, so the markup stays as it was.

::: {.value-box value-position="left" value="63"}
Left-positioned value, no title
:::

The title stays at the top even when the value is moved below the details, so
the order becomes title, details, value. Pinning that here because it is a
deliberate choice rather than a fallout.

::: {.value-box title="Bottomed" value-position="bottom" value="64"}
Title above, value below
:::

## Delta

::: {.value-box delta="+12%" value="17"}
Delta with an inferred up arrow, no colour override
:::

::: {.value-box delta="-8%" delta-color="#ff5252" value="18"}
Delta with an inferred down arrow and an explicit colour
:::

::: {.value-box delta="steady" value="19"}
No sign and no delta-direction means no arrow at all
:::

::: {.value-box delta="0%" delta-direction="flat" value="20"}
Explicit delta-direction overrides sign inference
:::

::: {.value-box delta="+5%" delta-font-size="1.3rem" delta-extra-style="font-style:italic;" value="21"}
Delta size and extra-style hooks
:::

A delta is escaped like any other text, not treated as raw HTML the way
value/title are — this must not become a live tag.

::: {.value-box delta="<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>" value="22"}
Delta cannot inject markup
:::

delta-direction is matched case-insensitively and, when set, overrides sign
inference — a mixed-case "Down" here must win over the "+" in the delta text.

::: {.value-box delta="+3%" delta-direction="Down" value="23"}
Mixed-case delta-direction overrides an inferred arrow
:::

An unrecognised delta-direction shows no arrow, with a warning, rather than
failing silently or crashing.

::: {.value-box delta="5%" delta-direction="sideways" value="24"}
Unrecognised delta-direction
:::

value-position="left"/"right" gives the value+delta pair flex-shrink:0 so it
holds its size next to details under space pressure, the same protection the
value alone already gets without a delta.

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" icon-size="1.5rem" value-position="left" delta="+9%" value="25"}
Delta combined with value-position=left
:::

## Explicitly blanked attributes

An empty string is truthy in Lua, so a blanked attribute is easy to mistake for
a set one and emit `font-size:;` from. These boxes exist so the "no empty CSS
declarations" assertion has something to bite on.

::: {.value-box icon="bi-star" icon-size="" icon-color="" value="14"}
Blank icon sizing and colour
:::

::: {.value-box height="" width="" align="" font-size="" value="15"}
Blank box sizing and alignment
:::
